questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors built on or after March 1, 1997 with air brakes must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: When doing the stop/start maneuver during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to get onto the shoulder.
Slam on the brakes to stop as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you will pull over to the shoulder and stop. Check traffic, use your turn signal, slow down smoothly with even braking, change gears as needed, and come to a full stop without coasting.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side.
Only use the mirror on the passenger's side.

questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors often when backing to see hazards behind your vehicle. Use a helper to watch blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: Before driving a bus, you must:

options.text: Review its most recent inspection report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review its most recent inspection report.
questions.explanation: Always inspect a bus before driving it. Review the inspection report from the previous driver. Only drive the bus if any listed defects have been repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: Emergency exit signs:

options.text: May sometimes be hidden by cargo on the bus.
Do not need to be displayed because the purpose of an emergency exit is always clear.
Should be clearly visible and identifiable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be clearly visible and identifiable.
questions.explanation: Emergency exit signs on a bus must always be clearly visible. The emergency door light must work properly.

questions.question: When an engine is started:

options.text: The brakes should be locked up.
Warning lights should come on and then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on and then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: If you must stop on the side of a highway, how far behind your vehicle should warning devices be placed?
questions.explanation: When stopping your truck on the side of a highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind the vehicle.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how to handle hazards safely if they become dangerous.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep one hand on the steering wheel and wave with the other hand.

questions.explanation: If a tire fails, braking can cause you to lose control. Avoid the brakes until your vehicle slows down on its own. Then brake gently, move off the road, and stop.

questions.question: When can you cross a drawbridge controlled by a traffic signal?

options.text: Only after stopping 50 feet before the bridge.
Only if other vehicles are crossing too.
Only after getting out to check conditions.

questions.explanation: When a drawbridge has a green traffic signal, you can slow down and proceed without stopping.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when you brake, what does it mean?

options.text: The brakes need to be serviced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be serviced.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you may have a brake problem. Get it fixed before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle is against the law.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should you use four-way flashers?

options.text: Turn them on before crossing railroad tracks.
Only near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross a railroad crossing. Turn them off once your entire vehicle has passed the tracks.

questions.question: What can drivers do during the basic control skills test?

options.text: Cannot stop and get out to check the vehicle's position.
Should try not to get out to check the vehicle's position.
Can get out only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Can get out only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can get out only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before getting out. You can check the vehicle's position up to twice, except during straight line backing when you can look only once.

questions.question: What does heavy steering often indicate?
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means one of your front tires has failed. If your steering feels different, safely exit the road and check your tires.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle can stop within the area you can see ahead. Slow down when you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leak for a triple combination air brake vehicle in one minute?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leak rate should not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Signs of brake damage include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin. Clean pads are normal and not a problem.
